1 Concerning his life, cf. Suter, Die Mathematiker und Astronomen der Araber, p. 28, no. 53; Dyroff in Boll, Sphaera, p. 482 ff.
2 Cf. Houzeau and Lancaster, Bibliographie génér. de l'astronomie, Brussels, 1887, vol. I, p. 702 ff.; Suter, loc. cit., p. 28 f.
3 You will find only four small fragments in Catal., vol. IV, p. 124 ff.
4 The same also exists in the Munich manuscript Clm. 826, f. 11 ff. (cf. Dyroff in Boll, Sphaera, p. 421) and in the Oxford manuscript (Houzeau and Lancaster, p. 704, no. 3844).
5 Albîrunî, The chronology of ancient nations, translated by Edward Sachau, London, 1879.
6 The Latin version in the Brussels manuscript similarly begins with the words f. 69: 'Aposaytes said I sent (sic) to Albumasar the nativity of the son of the king of the Indians'.

summary.headline: Mysteries of Apomasar
summary.text: Introduction to the Books of the Mysteries of Apomasar, identifying Abû Ma'šar and his disciple Šâdân as authors and comparing the Greek Angelicus text with a Latin version in Brussels manuscript 1464. It cites Albîrunî and Edward Sachau on a nativity calculation concerning Saturn’s decree of human lifespan and the king of India’s son.
